title: Quarter Gate Cruiseplan and All-Hands Rehearsal
summary: Working plan for the upcoming company all-hands + quarterly gate. Focus: align on OKR gating decisions, surface cross-org risks, rehearse exec talking points and fallback language for any rollout slips.
body:
Purpose:
- Create a compact, repeatable run-of-show and rehearsal plan we can execute in 7 business days before the quarter gate.
- Make sure executives and leads have concise talking points for OKR decisions (pass/adjust/defer) and the all-hands narrative.
- Surface and gate any cross-team blockers that would prevent committing to Q2 OKR launches.

Audience:
- All staff (town-hall) for the final all-hands.
- Exec + leads for the pre-briefing and OKR gating meeting.
- Engineering/product SROs for call-to-action items post-gate.

High-level objectives for the session:
1) Announce company-level OKR decisions with rationale and clear owner commit timelines.
2) Show top 3 product wins (hosted API latency improvements, Dedicated capacity milestones, Private deployment pilot kickoff) with measurable outcomes.
3) Share reliability heatmap and short-term mitigations for any risk buckets.
4) Launch a 30-day follow-through cadence with weekly progress checkpoints.

Agenda (All-Hands - 45 min):
- 0:00–0:05 Opening: CEO framing (Northstar + why we choose to accelerate/defer).
- 0:05–0:12 Exec spotlight: CTO (serving-runtime wins & performance benchmarks).
- 0:12–0:20 Product brief: VP Product (OKR gating decisions + customer impact).
- 0:20–0:30 Reliability & Ops: SRE lead (heatmap + mitigation plan).
- 0:30–0:36 Customer story: Solutions eng vignette (early Dedicated customer win).
- 0:36–0:42 People & org: Head of People (hiring tempo and role hotspots).
- 0:42–0:45 Closing: CEO (ask stack + how to get involved).

Run-of-show for Exec Pre-brief (30 min) — 1 day before all-hands:
- 0:00–0:05 Quick status + objective of the pre-brief.
- 0:05–0:12 OKR gate table: Proposed decisions (pass/adjust/defer) for each company-level OKR.
- 0:12–0:20 Risk callouts and mitigation commitments (SLOs, capacity, hiring).
- 0:20–0:28 Comms script review (CEO remarks + fallback lines).
- 0:28–0:30 Final sign-off and next steps.

OKR Gate Table (short form to be published):
- Objective A: "Unified inference performance" — Proposed: PASS (metrics: p50 latency down 18%, unit cost down 9%)
  - Rationale: Serving runtime landmarks merged; host benchmarks validated on prod-backed synthetic load.
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- Objective B: "Dedicated adoption & revenue" — Proposed: ADJUST
  - Rationale: Sales traction healthy but onboarding automation incomplete; shift to prioritized automation sprint in next 6 weeks.
  - Owner: product-dedicated + solutions-eng.
- Objective C: "Private deployment compliance" — Proposed: PASS (pilot contracts signed, initial on-prem package validated)
  - Owner: product-private + security-and-compliance.
- Objective D: "Developer experience & docs" — Proposed: DEFER
  - Rationale: Resource constraints; prioritize critical SDK fixes and console rollouts.
  - Owner: developer-experience.

Key messages and talk tracks (short bullets for slides):
- CEO: "We win by making inference predictable and economical — this quarter we focused investment where it moves the needle for customers and unit economics."
- CTO: "Technical wins: runtime optimizer now does kernel selection earlier in pipeline; continuous batching gives a predictable 15–25% cost reduction on long-tail workloads."
- VP Product: "We chose to adjust Dedicated rollout timing to avoid partial onboarding experiences — this preserves enterprise trust and ensures SLAs when we scale."
- SRE: "We measured availability drift at the tail — immediate mitigations: auto-failover tuning, extra capacity buffer during business hours, and tighter alert thresholds."

Slide/Deck notes (for presenter handoff):
- Slide 3 (metrics): include before/after graphs for p50/p95 latency and per-token cost; annotate with the exact experiment bucket names.
- Slide 6 (OKR gate): one-line rationale per OKR plus explicit "next milestone" and date.
- Slide 9 (risks): four risk cards — capacity, onboarding automation, security compliance, developer adoption — with owner & 2-week mitigation.

Rehearsal schedule (compressed 3-day plan):
- Day -3: Draft deck + one-pager published to linked_artifacts. Directors: sanity check content and numbers.
- Day -2: Slide lock and speaker notes due. Speaker rehearsal (30 min) with product and SRE leads.
- Day -1: Exec pre-brief + slide walkthrough (30 min). Run fallback Q&A.
- Day 0: All-hands run-of-show at 10:00 PT — AV test 09:40, host check 09:50.

Roles & responsibilities (quick matrix):
- Host: Marisol Rivera (ops) — start/stop timer, manage q&a queue.
- CEO speaker: Evan Park — main framing, closing.
- CTO speaker: Liam O'Sullivan — technical highlights and handoff to product.
- VP Product: Priya Nair — OKR gate details.
- SRE lead: Sanjay Mehta — reliability heatmap and mitigations.
- Deck custodian: Asha Patel — final deck version + post-event notes.

Pre-flight checklist (must be green before we go live):
- [ ] Deck version uploaded to drive and linked in event invite.
- [ ] Speaker notes reviewed + backup lines prepared for 3 likely tough Qs.
- [ ] OKR gate decisions ratified by execs (timestamped signoff in confluence link).
- [ ] PR/comm prerelease to customer-success for key customers.
- [ ] AV dry-run complete and remote presenters tested.

Risk register (top items):
- Onboarding automation gap (impact: delayed Dedicated revenue) — mitigation: triage to a 2-week sprint and provide manual onboarding playbook.
- Tail latency regressions under specific model families — mitigation: deploy fallback model variant routing and increase autoscaling threshold.
- Compliance checklist missing for one pilot customer — mitigation: security-and-compliance in checkpoint with legal by EOD.

Open questions (for exec decision during pre-brief):
- Do we publicly commit to the Dedicated launch date in the all-hands or keep it as "pilot phase" language? (tradeoff: sales expectations vs. risk of slip).
- If Product OKR is adjusted, how do we reallocate developer capacity to avoid blocking the runtime team?
- What is an acceptable unit-cost delta for early Dedicated customers to accept manual onboarding?

Post-event follow-up plan (owner + timeline):
- Publish brief notes to confluence + short recording clip within 24 hours — owner: Asha Patel.
- OKR adjustment tracker updated with owners and milestones within 48 hours — owner: VP Product (Priya Nair).
- Incident mitigation tickets created for any SRE items — owner: SRE lead (Sanjay Mehta).

Action Items (immediate):
- Priya: finalize adjusted OKR language and milestone dates by 2025-02-18.
- Liam: prepare p50/p95 charts with annotation and raw query names by 2025-02-17.
- Marisol: confirm AV setup and test participants list by 2025-02-19.
- Asha: assemble final deck, push to drive, and update linked_artifacts by 2025-02-19.

Notes to self / shorthand (working doc vibe):
- Keep message tight: 3 wins + 1 ask (join 30-day follow-up).
- Avoid deep dive on SDK roadmap in all-hands — channel to smaller forum unless critical.
- Prepare one customer quote for Dedicated to show traction.
- If we have to pivot messaging, use slide 6 (OKR gate) as the single source of truth.

Appendix (quick links and references):
- Benchmark bucket names: perf/ci/seq-len-512, perf/prod-longtail-02.
- Confluence pre-brief doc: confluence:CO/Q2-bridge-notes-1423
- Slack thread for live q&a moderation: slack:#allhands-runbook-thread

End of draft.

-- Asha (owner)
notes: Work-in-progress; expect edits after director sanity check. This is a living rehearsal and gate plan — please add line edits directly in the drive deck or comment in the linked confluence doc.
